description:
Start an AI verification session from a prompt

Starts an AI verification session from a plain-language prompt and optional dataPoints/loginUrls; returns the session with verificationUrl to share with the user. Needs the org token and at least one active callback subscription (409 otherwise; a webhook with 5 consecutive failures doesn't count). It proves only values the page shows. For an internal ID, or a value that appears only in an API response, create a provider instead. No provider or org keypair needed: Builder manages the AI app key. Poll with get_ai_verification_session or wait_for_ai_session.

body.description: Body for `POST /verifications/ai-sessions`. Send a `prompt`, at least one entry in `dataPoints`, or both.

context.description: Values you already know, such as `{"fullName": "Asha Rao"}`. Builder merges them over the values the prompt states and returns the result in `context`. Must not contain `attestationNonce` or `attestationNonceData`; bind those after you create the session. Also must not contain `reclaimSessionId`, `extractedParameters`, or `builderSessionId`. Omit if you have none.

dataPoints.description: The values to verify. Required unless you send a `prompt`. Names must be unique, and at least one data point must be required (its `isOptional` is `false` or absent). When you send data points, Builder keeps them and adds only optional data points that the prompt implies. When you send none, Builder chooses the data points from the prompt. Every required data point must appear in the verified proofs. If one is missing, the session ends as `rejected` with `reasonCode` `missing-data-points`.

description.description: What the value is and why it proves the claim.

isOptional.description: Defaults to `false`. If `true`, the claim can be proven without this value, and the proofs can omit it. If `false` or absent, the data point is required, and a session whose proofs omit it ends as `rejected` with `reasonCode` `missing-data-points`.

name.description: Name of the value, such as `username`. Starts with a letter or underscore, followed by up to 63 letters, digits, or underscores.

source.description: Email verification only. Marks this data point as a verified email fact that Builder fills from the cryptographically verified proof — `email.sender` (the From address), `email.recipient` (the connected recipient), `email.date` (the signed Date), or `email.signingDomain` (the DKIM signing domain) — instead of asking the AI to extract it from the email body. Omit for a content data point the AI extracts; when omitted, Builder may infer it from the prompt and description.

geoLocation.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as `IN`. Builder searches the web from this country (Google's `gl` parameter), so portals for that country rank first. If you omit it, the search has no country preference.

isEmailVerificationAllowed.description:
Defaults to `false`. If `true`, the share page offers to verify with an email from the brand:
- when Builder isn't sure where the user signs in (several pages,
  or one page whose confidence is at most 1 minus the minimum
  email fit: 0.3 by default, set per session by the
  `builder.aiEmailMinConfidence` feature flag);

- when the prompt suggests the value usually arrives by email
  (tickets, bookings, orders, receipts, subscriptions, statements,
  invoices, shipping, enrollment or admission confirmations,
  transcripts, student or membership ID cards), even next to a page
  you sent in `loginUrls`;

- when the website start fails;
- when the website verification fails, in which case the session
  stays open until the user verifies by email, gives up, or the
  session expires.

If no login page is found, the session becomes `ready` with no `candidates`. If you omit it, the page doesn't offer email.
Only the brand's own email counts. Builder takes the brand's domains from the prompt and the lookup. Mail that an event or ticketing platform (such as Luma) sends for the brand counts only from the event's organizer. Builder finds the organizer on the brand's site (named in the prompt, or found by search and linked to and from the platform's event listing), on the event's listing page, or on a platform page that the prompt names. When the email comes from a platform, name the sender's address or the platform's event or organizer page URL in the prompt, such as `from devfestmumbai@calendar.luma-mail.com` or `from https://luma.com/luh11tqc`.

loginUrls.description: Pages where the user signs in, such as `https://portal.example.edu/login`. Builder shows them first as candidates with source `caller`, and skips the web search. Each URL must use `http` or `https`, can't contain credentials, and must resolve to a public host. If the prompt suggests the value usually arrives by email and `isEmailVerificationAllowed` is `true`, the user still sees the choice next to these pages.

prompt.description: What to verify, in plain language, such as "verify I'm a student at Manipal University". Required unless `dataPoints` has at least one item. Builder rejects a prompt that contains credentials, card numbers, instructions for the AI, or a sensitive claim. The prompt and the data point lines together can't exceed 10,000 characters.

verificationClientUrl.description: Base URL of the registered verification client the user verifies with, as for `POST /verifications/sessions`. Builder charges this client's quota pool. If you omit it, Builder uses the default (`portals`) client.

orgToken.description: The organization API key (`rorg_…`) this call authenticates with: from `issue_org_token`, or the app's RECLAIM_ORG_SECRET. Defaults to the MCP server's RECLAIM_ORG_SECRET. Never echo it back to the user.

name: create_ai_verification_session
